decision.summary: The tenant reports the washing machine repair, closed on 28 Feb, failed within days. I reopened the job, asked Lantern Services for a no-charge guarantee return visit, held their £75.11 invoice, and updated the tenant and landlord. A follow-up is set for 7 March.

answers.question: Where does this case stand right now, and what is outstanding?
answers.answer: It was closed on 28 Feb with no photos, no tenant confirmation and an invoice outstanding. The tenant says the fix failed. It is now reopened and waiting on Lantern to confirm a return visit. The invoice is on hold.

answers.question: What is the next action, who is it for, and through which channel?
answers.answer: The guarantee return-visit instruction went to Lantern Services by email. The tenant and landlord have also been updated by email. A follow-up on 7 March checks the visit date.

answers.question: Does anything need a human decision, and why?
answers.answer: No. This is a routine guarantee return visit. Any chargeable work or the invoice outcome would come back to the landlord or a human later.

args.body:
Dear Lantern Services,

Flat 20, 120 Alder Lane (NBL-042): the tenant reports the washing machine repair (heating element wiring, your visit in late Feb) has not held. It worked for a couple of washes, and the water has not heated on the 60°C cycle for about 5 days.

Please treat this as a return visit under your workmanship guarantee, at no extra charge. Please contact the tenant (same contact details as before, 07700 900566, enter the code when calling) to arrange a visit, and reply with the date you confirm. Please report what you find, with photos, and tell us if the heating element or thermostat needs replacing, along with the machine's age and any warranty terms. Do not start any chargeable work without our approval. Your invoice of £75.11 is on hold until this is resolved.

Thank you.
